title: Cryptologic Language Analyst (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DIR INTEL
raw_text:
7.     MOS 2641, Cryptologic Language Analyst (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DIR INTEL

    a. Summary. Cryptologic Language Analysts (CLA) monitor, transcribe,
and translate intercepted target foreign communications; exploit every phase
of designated foreign communications by engaging in collection, processing,
exploitation, analysis, and reporting; and install, operate, and perform
preventive maintenance of program of record as well as commercially acquired
intercept equipment. Duties encompass all facets of signals intelligence
(SIGNT), electronic warfare (EW) and cyber operations in support of the MAGTF
at both team and battalion levels and must be prepared to contribute to each
as deemed necessary by the unit commander. Marines shall periodically
(annually or biennially, dependent on scores) retake the defense language
proficiency test (DLPT) and shall maintain a minimum proficiency of listening
2/reading (L2/R2) DLPT in their assigned 27XX language(s), in accordance with
reference (bb). Formal intermediate and advanced language training is
available and will be afforded to CLAs no later than upon PCS from their
first duty station. Per DoDI 3300.07, CLAs will engage, during normal duty
hours, a minimum of 160 hours of formal language training every 24 months.
MOS 2629, SIGINT/EW/CO Technician, is assigned upon promotion to staff
sergeant. Marines shall maintain language proficiency in their assigned 27XX
language(s) upon assignment of MOS 2629.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) No speech or hearing defects.

            (3) Must meet the requirements for EMOS 2712 to 2796.

            (4) Must possess a CL score of 110 or GT score of 105 or higher.

        (5) Must successfully complete a counter-intelligence scope polygraph
examination.

        (6) Security requirement: must have a current single scope
background investigation/T5 investigation and adjudicated for sensitive
compartmented information (SCI) eligibility.




                                          3-161                      Enclosure (1)
 3122                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



        (7) Must take the Defense Language Proficiency Test (DLPT) in the
Marine's assigned 27XX language(s) and maintain a minimum proficiency of L2/
R2 in accordance with reference (bb).

        (8) Graduation from a basic language course at the Defense Language
Institute (DLI). Basic Language Course may be waived if significant
proficiency in an appropriate language is demonstrated by achieving minimum
level 2 proficiency on the listening and reading portions of the DLPT in
accordance with reference (bb). Assignment to DLI requires a minimum score
of 100 or higher on the defense language aptitude battery (DLAB). The DLAB
score may be waived on a case-by-case basis if significant foreign language
experience is demonstrated, or a GT score over 110 is achieved and if such a
waiver is requested by the recruit screening office at the applicable Marine
Corps Recruiting Depot and approved by Headquarters Marine Corps,
Intelligence Division. For Marines executing a lateral move into this MOS,
the waiver request will originate with the marine's career planner and will
be approved by the 2641 specialist at intelligence division.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Complete the requirements for assignment of an EMOS 2712-2796.

        (2) Complete the Basic Signals Operators Course (BSOC) (F07CVT1), San
Angelo, TX.

        (3) Complete one of the following Cryptologic Language requirements
for the associated 27XX EMOS:

            (a) Marines assigned EMOS 2712 through 2717 and 2728 through 2731
must complete the Middle East Cryptologic Linguist-Arabic Course (F072911),
or the Apprentice Cryptologic Linguist Specialist Non-Target Course
(F07CXE1).

            (b) Marines assigned EMOS 2736 through 2737 must complete the
Apprentice Cryptologic Analyst-Chinese Course (F072931), or the Apprentice
Cryptologic Linguist Specialist Non-Target Course (F07CXE1).

            (c) Marines assigned EMOS 2741 must complete the Asian-Pacific
Cryptologic Linguist-Korean Course (F072971), or the Apprentice Cryptologic
Linguist Specialist Non-Target Course (F07CXE1).

            (d) Marines assigned EMOS 2791 must complete Central Asian
Cryptologic Linguist-Russian Course (F0729A1), or the Apprentice Cryptologic
Linguist Specialist Non-Target Course (F07CXE1).

            (e) Marines assigned EMOS 2768 must complete the European
Cryptologic Linguist-Spanish Course (F0729C1), or the Apprentice Cryptologic
Linguist Specialist Non-Target Course (F07CXE1).

            (f) Marines assigned EMOS 2773 must complete the Voice
Interceptor Persian-Farsi Course (F07CXF1), or the Apprentice Cryptologic
Linguist Specialist Non-Target Course (F07CXE1).

            (g) Marines assigned EMOS 2772 must complete the Pashto
Supplemental Cryptologic Language Course (F07RHQ1), or the Apprentice
Cryptologic Linguist Specialist Non-Target Course (F07CXE1).




                                        3-162                        Enclosure (1)
 3122                                                             NAVMC 1200.1L



            (h) Marines assigned any EMOS 2712 through 2796 not listed in
paragraphs (a) through (g) must complete the Apprentice Cryptologic Linguist
Specialist Non-Target Course (F07CXE1).

    d. Duties.    For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (p), Signals Intelligence Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Interpreters and Translators 27-3091.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) SIGINT/EW/CO Technician, 2629.

            (2) Advanced Cryptologic Language Analyst, 2642.

            (3) SIGINT/EW/CO Chief, 2691.
common_text: CYCBERSPACE OPERATIONS 1. Introduction. The Signals Intelligence (SIGINT), Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) OccFld includes the employment of SIGINT, EW, support to cyberspace operations (CO) and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) systems engineering capabilities. Marines in this field are required to set up and operate collection and communications electronic equipment, manage intelligence data, prepare EW and intelligence reports, extend and mesh intelligence services, conduct preventive maintenance on assigned equipment, execute electromagnetic attack (EA), and assist in the operational control and management of SIGINT/EW/CO personnel, equipment, and facilities. Entry- level jobs include Communications Intelligence/Electromagnetic Warfare Operator, Signals Intelligence/Electromagnetic Warfare Analyst, Intelligence Surveillance Reconnaissance Systems Engineer, and Cryptologic Language Analyst. Marines can LATMOV into the 2600 OccFld at the grade of corporal or sergeant. Sergeants requesting LATMOV into the 2600 OccFld must have no more than 1 year time in grade. Duty assignments include Marine Forces Special Operations Command (MARSOC), Marine Corps Information Command (MCIC), Marine Forces Cyber Command (MARFORCYBER), Marine Cryptologic Support Battalion (MCSB), radio battalions, intelligence battalions, infantry battalions, littoral combat team (LCT), marine littoral regiments (MLR), and the staff sections of the MEF information groups (MIG), Marine divisions (MARDIV), and Marine aviation wings (MAW).

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
